identity.description:
Resume a stopped label run (label --resume)

`pr-review label --resume`: a label run that stops keeps each finding that reached a result, and a second run labels only the findings that are missing or that have a failed run.

## Why

On 2026-11-12, Codex reached its usage limit during the D4b R3 labeling. Case `pool-pr-review-44` kept 5 of its 9 labels, and two cases were not labeled. Without a resume, each new run labels every finding again and pays every Claude call again.

## What changes

- With `--resume`, the labeler reads the `labels.json` of each case in the output directory. It reuses a finding when its runs all completed, its text matches (file, lines, claim), and the labeling input is the same: run count, model ids, policy text and the labeler prompt files.
- Every run now writes a `digest` of that input in `labels.json`. A file with another digest, or with none, gives no reuse, and the run says so on stderr. So the `labels.json` files of the stopped R3 run give no reuse: they have no digest.
- The scorer cost counts only new calls. The summary names the reused findings per case.
- `labels.json`, `disagreements.json` and `human-queue.json` are written through a temp file and a rename.
- README, and the version goes to 0.10.0.

## Tests

`test/label-resume.test.ts` runs the CLI with a fake SDK client and a fake `codex`. `npm test` (1415), lint, typecheck, build and the version check pass.

triage.summary: Adds a --resume flag to `pr-review label`. labels.json now stores a digest of the labeling input (run count, model ids, policy, prompts). On resume, findings whose runs all completed and whose text is unchanged are reused without model calls, and the others are relabeled. Case files are written atomically, the summary lists the reused indexes, and the version is bumped to 0.10.0.

findings.claim: No test covers the error paths for a labels.json that is not JSON or that is not a labels file.

first.rationale: The guard is there. No test in label-resume.test.ts or label-cli.test.ts runs `--resume` together with `--format json`. The claim is true, but it is a minor coverage gap for a one-line guard that is easy to see.

escalated.rationale: The reuse lines print only when the summary has a `reused` field, which is set only with `--resume`. The one test that parses stdout as JSON (label-cli.test.ts) runs without `--resume`, and test/label-resume.test.ts never passes `--format`. So if someone removes the table-only guard, no test fails. This is a real but minor coverage gap around a simple guard.
